input.brief: Emilia makes handmade decorative hat-boxes of artificial flowers - dusty pink roses, mauve chrysanthemums, burlap and lace bows, cream velvet boxes; each one unique, lasts for years

direction.name: The specimen catalogue
direction.idea: Present what is on offer the way a field guide presents birds: each item alone on a flat colour, same scale, same angle, named plainly. A bakery's pastries become specimens and the specimens become the menu. A furniture maker's chairs each get their own colour tile. The format flatters ordinary objects because it treats each as worth looking at, and it replaces both the feature grid and the product-card grid with something that has a point of view.
direction.composition: Hero: a left-aligned statement of what this is (5–7vw, upper-left) beside or above a tight cluster of four to seven specimen tiles of different sizes arranged as a loose mosaic that runs off the right edge. Each tile is a flat colour square or 4:5 rectangle with one photograph centred on it, no border, 8–12px gaps. The main section is the catalogue itself: a grid of tiles in which each item has its name and one fact set beneath the tile in the text face, aligned left to the tile edge. Tile colours rotate through three or four fields from the palette. One tile in every six or seven is double size. Supporting sections (about, how to order) are plain text on the ground colour, kept short.
direction.typography: Friendly and plain. Item names at 18–22px in medium weight, facts beneath in the soft ink. One big statement in the hero; no other display type.
direction.colour: The tiles are the colour: three or four flat fields from the palette, repeated in a steady rotation. Ground stays neutral.
direction.imagery: Photographs of single items on plain backgrounds, all cropped to sit at the same apparent size within their tile. On light tiles, `mix-blend-mode: multiply` removes white studio backgrounds. If the subject's own item photographs are missing, use the dealt set and say so.
direction.richness: Rhythm of colour tiles and the pleasure of comparing like with like.
direction.pitfalls: It needs at least six items that can be shown as objects; with three it is a feature row. Keep labels outside the tiles. No shadows under the objects, no hover lift.

hero.name: Single specimen with name list
hero.blueprint: Borrowed from a museum plinth. A calm light ground with roughly 70% left empty. The wordmark is set large for a logo, about 28% of the viewport wide (clamp(64px, 6vw, 92px), heavy serif or grotesk), top-left on a 56px margin; one sentence of description at 15px sits top-right on the same margin, its first line aligned to the top of the wordmark. Dead centre stands one specimen: a flat tile in a palette colour, 400px wide and 460px tall (columns 5-8) with a 16px radius, holding a single cut-out item at about 80% of the tile height, object-fit: contain. Left of the tile, in columns 2-4, a vertical list of item names is right-aligned towards it: the selected name in full ink at 20px, the names above and below stepping down in size and opacity (18, 16, 14px; 60, 35, 15%). Choosing a name swaps the item and the tile colour. Below the tile, centred: the item's one-line fact at 14px, then the single action, a filled rectangle 240px wide. Three text links sit bottom-left at 14px.
hero.mobile: The wordmark sits top-left at 11vw with the description sentence beneath it at 15px. The tile takes the full width inside 20px margins at 4:5, starting at 30% of the height. The name list becomes one horizontal row under the tile that scrolls sideways with scroll-snap, the selected name centred in full ink at 18px. The action sits full width at the bottom of the screen; the links move to the footer.
hero.headline: The name itself as an oversized wordmark, up to 10 characters on one line; there is no separate statement.

type.note: A contemporary slab with smooth curves and unbracketed serifs, even enough to carry headings and paragraphs alike. Suits developer tools, personal sites, open-source and nonprofit projects.

palette.name: Stone and blueprint
palette.note: Stone paper carries the whole page with near-black and grey text. One image at a time is printed in the accent blue as its only ink, and the same blue fills the single button.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Statement with inline thumbnails
sections.blueprint: A centred statement of 18–28 words, four lines at clamp(32px, 4.2vw, 62px), medium or bold weight, leading 1.12, in a block 60–66% of the viewport wide with 22vh of empty ground above and below. Three to five small frames sit inline between words: each is an `inline-block` 0.85em tall and 0.85–1.3em wide, `vertical-align: -0.1em`, radius 0.14em, holding a tightly cropped photograph (or a crop of real interface) of the thing the neighbouring word names. Frames are part of the line, never floating over it, with 0.12em of space either side. No heading above and no paragraph below; the statement is set as a `p`. Directly under the section the page may split into two flat colour halves or begin the first product row, so the thumbnails read as a preview of what follows. On a motif-driven page every frame takes the motif's shape.
sections.mobile: Left-aligned instead of centred, at 8vw with leading 1.15, about seven lines inside 20px margins. Keep at most three inline frames, each exactly one cap-height tall, and make sure none lands at the start of a line. Vertical padding drops to 96px.

sections.name: Staggered tiles, empty cells
sections.blueprint: A four-column grid with 16px gutters and 5vw margins in which tiles snap to columns but vary in span and height, and some cells are deliberately left empty. Pattern for eight projects: row one, a wide tile spanning columns 1–2 at 3:2 and a single tile in column 4 at 4:5, column 3 empty; row two, single tiles in columns 2 and 3, columns 1 and 4 empty; row three, a wide tile in columns 3–4 and a single in column 1. Each tile is a photograph, or a project image centred with 12% padding on a flat pastel or dark ground from the palette. Square corners, or one consistent shape detail such as a large radius on the bottom-right corner only. Under each tile one caption row at 14px: project name left, year and category right. The heading, two words stacked at clamp(40px, 4.5vw, 68px), occupies the empty cell of row one.
sections.mobile: Two columns with 10px gutters. Wide tiles span both columns; single tiles alternate left and right with the other cell left empty beside every second one, so the stagger survives. The heading sits above at 10vw. Captions stack the name over the year.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: Tiles that grow
sections.blueprint: Order is carried by size. Three flat colour tiles stand in one row, bottom-aligned (align-items: end) with 10px gaps, each larger than the one before: columns 1–3 at 30vh tall, columns 4–7 at 44vh, columns 8–12 at 60vh. Each tile holds one photograph of the subject at that stage (raw, in progress, finished), centred and scaled so the object grows from tile to tile; on light tiles mix-blend-mode: multiply removes a white studio background. One palette colour per tile. Text sits under the tiles, outside them, aligned to each tile's left edge: a stage name at 20px medium whose wording carries the order ('Picked', 'Pressed', 'Poured') and two lines at 16px in the soft ink. The heading, two to four words at 40–52px, occupies the empty ground above the two smaller tiles, top-aligned with the tallest tile. A fourth stage is possible with spans of 2, 3, 3 and 4 columns.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack in order and grow in height instead: 34vw, 46vw and 62vw tall, each at full width. The name and text sit under each tile at 18px and 16px. The heading comes first at 30px. 28px between stages.

sections.name: The itemised receipt
sections.blueprint: For offers made of parts: a base price plus options, a kit, a bundle. A tall paper-coloured slip 380px wide sits in columns 8–11 on a contrasting ground, its bottom edge cut into a zigzag with `clip-path: polygon()`, its top edge running off the top of the section. On the slip, with 28px padding: the name centred at 20px bold, then each item as a row with the description left and the amount right at 16px with tabular figures, 14px between rows; a thick 4px bar in the ink colour; then the total as the largest thing on the slip at 44px, right-aligned. Columns 1–6 carry the heading (two to four words at about 4vw), one paragraph at 18px and the button, starting 96px from the top. If options are selectable, ticking one in the left column adds its row to the slip and updates the total.
sections.mobile: Heading, paragraph and any options come first. The slip follows at 86% width, centred, keeping its zigzag foot, with rows at 16px and the total at 36px. The button sits under the slip at full width, 52px tall.

sections.name: Accordion of filled tiles
sections.blueprint: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, `position: sticky; top: 96px` so it stays while the list scrolls past. Columns 5–12 hold the accordion: each question is a filled tile one step from the page ground, with 8px between tiles, no border and the page's one radius (or its motif's corner). A closed tile is 72px tall with the question at 20px medium on the left, 24px padding, and on the right a plus sign drawn from two 3px bars 16px long. The open tile switches to the accent colour with its assigned ink, the plus becomes a minus by rotating one bar, and the answer appears at 17px, no wider than 52ch. Build each tile as `<details>` with a shared `name` so one opens at a time. Six to nine tiles.
sections.mobile: The heading sits above at 9vw, not sticky. Tiles run full width with 6px gaps, questions at 18px wrapping to two lines, closed height at least 64px. The open tile keeps the accent colour, and answers are set at 16px with 20px padding.

sections.name: Clip-out coupon form
sections.blueprint: The form is a coupon to cut out. One filled card in a strong flat colour, about 2.2:1, spans columns 2–11 with a 14px radius, with 120px of ground above and below. Semicircular notches 28px across are cut into its top and bottom edges at the 46% mark with `clip-path` or an SVG `mask`, and a vertical row of round dots (a dotted `border-left` 5px thick in the ground colour) joins the two notches as the perforation. Left of the perforation, with 48px padding: a two-line heading of three to five words at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px) in heavy capitals at the top, and one sentence at 16px at the bottom. Right of it: four inputs stacked with 10px gaps, each a filled block 52px tall in a lighter tone of the card with its placeholder at 16px, then a full-width solid submit bar 56px tall in the darkest ink. Inputs keep visually hidden `label` elements.
sections.mobile: The card turns upright and spans the width with 12px margins. The perforation becomes horizontal: notches on the left and right edges, dots across. Heading and sentence sit above it; the four inputs and the submit bar sit below, each 54px tall.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Noho
references.idea: Furniture sold through people misusing it (wearing, balancing on, hiding behind chairs on flat colour backdrops) while the interface stays quiet beige.
references.hero: The viewport splits exactly 50/50 by tone alone: left half warm off-white, right half a slightly darker greige, no rule. Left: a small lowercase logo top-left at 30px margin, then a four-line bold headline at 60px (4.2vw), tracking -0.04em and leading near 1.0, top-left aligned and filling the upper 40%; the lower half is empty except for a one-line 18px tagline pinned bottom-left. Right: a staggered mosaic of seven portrait photos, each about 175 by 230px with 15px gaps, on a four-column, three-row grid with several cells left empty and the rightmost image cropped by the viewport edge. A white square menu button sits top-right.
references.type: Switzer only. Headlines weight 600, tracking -0.04em, sentence case, charcoal rather than black; statements at 60px, body 13.5px, meta labels about 11px grey. The digest records one element at 15.6vw. Roughly four sizes, one family, no caps.
references.colour: #f1eee9 #e7e2dc #cdc0b0 #3c3c3c #b4a5db #f2e05a — The interface is three close warm beiges with charcoal type; saturated colour (lilac, yellow, olive, terracotta, sand) exists only in photo backdrops and the products themselves.
references.imagery: Studio shots of people interacting oddly with chairs on seamless single-colour backdrops, portrait 3:4, square corners; plus very large cut-out product shots on beige with a soft radial glow and contact shadow, cropped by the panel edge.
references.layout: Outer margins of 16-30px. Sections alternate between split halves, centred statements and left-aligned headings over card rows. Cards are flat rectangles one tone darker than the page with 8px gaps, content pinned to the top-left and bottom edges. Wide empty bands separate sections.

sections.description: A centred four-line statement at about 60px bold with tiny square photo thumbnails, roughly one cap-height tall, dropped inline between words like emoji. Directly beneath, the page splits into two full-width flat colour halves (light greige and tan), each with a small circled plus button in its top inner corner; these are the tops of the two product panels.

Two side-by-side panels in different beiges, each dominated by one enormous cut-out chair (one yellow, one black) cropped at the top so mostly seat and legs show, with a soft radial highlight behind. Along the bottom of each panel: a tiny label and price at left, a row of colour-swatch dots, then two small rectangular buttons at right, one white and one charcoal.

Three equal flat tiles in a row with 8px gaps, each about 210px tall. One short claim is centred in each at roughly 18px, and an index number sits alone in the bottom-left corner in 11px. A small bulleted label hangs above each tile. After a large empty gap, another centred bold statement begins.

A horizontal strip of colour-backdrop photos bleeds off both edges at the top of the section. Below, a left-aligned bold heading at about 40px, then a row of beige cards overflowing to the right: each has an @name at top-left, a short paragraph in 11px, and a bottom row with star glyphs left and a small text link right.

steal: Split the hero 50/50 by background tone alone, park the headline top-left and one tagline bottom-left, and fill the other half with a staggered photo mosaic that leaves grid cells empty.
Keep the interface in three close beige tones and confine all saturated colour to photo backdrops and products, so the photography becomes the palette.
Drop cap-height photo thumbnails inline between the words of a large centred statement.

references.name: Madie
references.idea: A burgundy-and-cream bakery brand in which the madeleines themselves, cut out like specimens, become the menu.
references.hero: A dark, warm photograph (iced coffee with a logo sticker and a glazed madeleine on a wooden counter, burgundy tiles behind) fills a rounded-corner frame inset 20px from every edge on a cream page; the subject sits right of centre. In the left column, starting 42% down: a small star-rating line, then a three-line uppercase headline at 5vw in a heavy geometric sans, the first two lines outline-only and the third solid cream, a three-line paragraph, and a row with a pink pill button and an underlined text link. Top-left: menu icon and script logo. Top-right: a three-language pill toggle. Bottom-right: a circular text badge.
references.type: Dazzle, a heavy geometric uppercase, for headlines at 72px, used both solid and as an outline stroke; Cottorway, a slightly wide geometric sans, for 14px body and for a light italic accent word. A brush-script logo. Tracked capitals near 10px for labels.
references.colour: #f6efe6 #3d0012 #5c0a23 #ff99d3 #160b0a #e8a530 — Cream and deep burgundy alternate by section across wavy boundaries. Bubblegum pink is reserved for buttons, the active filter pill and carousel arrows; the product cut-outs supply every other colour.
references.imagery: A moody warm-graded hero photo; individual madeleines shot from above and cut out with soft shadows as small menu thumbnails; white line drawings (dog in beret, cafe table); rounded photo cards stacked at a tilt; a map redrawn in burgundy.
references.layout: Centred intro, a left-anchored story block on burgundy, then a two-column menu inside a container about 60% of the width. Section edges are curved waves rather than straight lines. Rounded frames and a sticky header with filter pills recur throughout.

sections.description: Cream field, everything centred. A tiny tracked-capitals label flanked by two short rules, then a two-line heading: the first line outlined uppercase in burgundy at about 4.5vw, the second a lowercase light italic of the body sans, solid. Three short paragraphs at 13px follow in a column about 45% wide. The section ends in a burgundy wave rising from the bottom, with a white line-drawn dog perched on the curve.

Burgundy field patterned with a faint tone-on-tone repeat of the logo. Left: a white line illustration, a three-line paragraph with bold phrases, two round pink arrow buttons and a slide counter. Right: a stack of portrait photo cards with rounded corners, the top one tilted a few degrees and the others fanned behind it. The bottom edge curves back to cream.

A sticky row of three pill filters beside the logo, the active one filled pink. Each category has an outlined uppercase label at left, an item count at far right and a hairline beneath. Items run in two columns: a 60px cut-out madeleine at left, then a bold uppercase name and a two-to-three-line italic description; some carry a tiny best-seller note or a pink allergen tag. No prices and no boxes.

Deep burgundy. The left two-thirds is an interactive map restyled entirely in burgundy and pink with rounded corners, the script logo as its pin and a small address card overlaid bottom-left. The right third is a rounded outlined panel listing opening hours, phone and email under tiny capital labels, plus two social icons. The script logo, large and white, is centred below, followed by a tracked-capitals legal line.

steal: Set a headline with its first lines as outline strokes and the last line solid, so emphasis falls on the final phrase without a size change.
Replace the stock map with one restyled in the brand's two colours and use the logo as the pin.
Build the menu from small cut-out product photos beside bold names and italic notes in two columns, with no cards.

references.name: longbow
references.idea: The page is built on a visible four-column construction grid with square handles at every intersection, and cars, glass cards and a giant condensed marquee are slotted into its cells like objects on a designer's artboard.
references.hero: Mid-grey studio video of two roadsters fills the viewport inside a thin outer frame. White hairlines split it into four equal columns and two rows, with small white square nodes at each crossing. A frosted-glass nav bar sits top centre spanning the two middle columns: hamburger left, condensed wordmark centre, a mono models link right. Bottom left, a white condensed marquee of the brand name at 21vw, a third of viewport height, runs off the left edge and stops at the centre line. The bottom-right cell holds a small glass tag, a two-line serif headline with the second line italic, and a six-line uppercase mono paragraph.
references.type: Bebas Neue at 21vw with -0.06em tracking for marquee words; EB Garamond near 28px, light, with italic second lines for headings; Geist Mono 13px uppercase for all body and labels. Three faces with strict roles and a roughly 23-times jump from body to display.
references.colour: #888c8f #a8a7a9 #ffffff #1b1b1c #1f5c49 #b5552e — One mid grey for both page and studio backdrop with white type throughout; colour comes only from the product: racing-green paint, tan leather, red tail lamps. One black video band late in the page.
references.imagery: Studio renders and video of cars on a seamless grey backdrop that matches the page colour, cropped tight to noses, tails and badges; images are square-cornered and sized exactly to grid cells or run full bleed.
references.layout: Four equal columns with visible hairlines and node markers persist down the whole 18-screen page. Content occupies one or two cells at a time and leaves the others as flat grey; giant marquee words and full-bleed car frames alternate with small serif-plus-mono text cells.

sections.description: A full-bleed close-up of one car fills the viewport. A dark frosted-glass card exactly one column wide and about half the viewport tall sits over the image in the second column: centred serif model name with an italic edition line, a mono price line, a small landscape thumbnail of the car and a white square-cornered button. The next model repeats the layout with the card shifted to the third column.

Flat grey screen. A giant white condensed marquee line runs across the top, partly behind the nav. In the first column: a tiny rounded index tag, a two-line serif heading with italic second line, then after a gap a ten-line uppercase mono paragraph. In the third column a tall portrait crop of bodywork and badge fills one cell from the marquee down. The other two columns stay empty.

Between sections, three condensed white words about a third of the viewport high are distributed across the grid columns with wide gaps between them and cropped by the viewport bottom, acting as a divider between a full-bleed car frame and the next text block. Grid lines and nodes run over the letters.

A black band holds a wide video frame inset from left and right by black bars, showing a motion-blurred car head-on on a road in a cool teal grade; the grid lines and nodes continue over it and the grey page resumes below. A single-line uppercase mono legal ticker runs along the very bottom edge of the page.

steal: Draw the layout grid as visible hairlines with small square nodes at intersections and size every image and card to exact cells.
Match the page background to the photo backdrop colour so product shots merge with the page and only the product carries colour.
Give three faces fixed jobs: a condensed sans only at 20vw for marquees, a light serif with an italic second line for headings, uppercase mono for all body text.
